newsitem.title: UK: Door closing fast on UK rate cuts - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Door closing fast on UK rate cuts - analysts.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's apparant decision to leave UK interest rates on hold on Thursday could mean the window of opportunity for another cut has slammed shut, analysts said.
"Rates are unlikely to be cut again this cycle and will now remain on hold for some time," said Ian Stewart, UK economist at Merrill Lynch.
"As time goes by more data will point to economic strength, not just on the consumer side but also in the corporate sector and the arguments for another rate cut will get flimsier."

The Bank of England dealt at unchanged rates in early money market operations. Although it could cut interest rates later, recent practice suggests rates will now stay on hold until the next monetary meeting on September 23.

James Barty, chief UK economists at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said tentative signs of a recovery in manufacturing sector and the Bank of England's hawkish stance on policy probably persuaded Clarke to leave rates on hold.
"The two main factors behind the decision are that the economy is firming and the Bank has already said the next move in rates should be up."
But Barty said the time is fast approachihng when the Bank will put pressur on Clarke to rasie rates.
"At some time, probably before the general election, there will be pressure on Clarke to raise rates, so he's keeping his powder dry to help reflect that pressure."
The Bank of England opposed the last quarter-point rate cut in June which took base rates down to 5.75 percent.

Since then, it has hardened its line further and at the time of its last inflation report in July chief economist Mervyn King said that Bank officials would discuss the merits of a pre- emptive rate rise before this week's meeting.
The general election must be held by May 1997.

The ruling Conservatives still trailing Labour in the opinion polls by over 20 points and some analysts had speculated Clarke would be tempted to cut rates again to give the economy one last push before the polls.
But a small group of economists still forecast another rate cut.

"RPI data is going to be very favourable over the next few months which will change the outlook for inflation and give Clarke scope for for another easing," said Ian Shepherdson, chief UK economist at HSBC Markets.
Shepherdson said he was not surprised Clarke left rates on hold this month. "It's too soon after the last rate cut and too soon after the Bank's inflation report."
He forecasts Clarke may even leave it until after the budget which he will deliver on November 26.
